name: MCPJam Inspector error class spiking (prod)
aplQuery: | extend fpSource = coalesce(tostring(errorMessage), tostring(errorCode), strcat(tostring(route), ' ', tostring(statusCode)))
| summarize recent = countif(_time > ago(1h)), baseline = countif(_time <= ago(1h)), orgs = dcountif(orgId, _time > ago(1h)), maxStatus = maxif(toint(statusCode), _time > ago(1h)) by fp
| where recent > 1000 or (maxStatus >= 500 and recent > 100) or (recent >= 20 and orgs >= 3 and recent > 20 * baseHourly)
description: PAGE — owner: marcelo. One error class is running far above its own 14-day baseline.

THE PRECEDENT: 2026-08-06, 3,705 failures in one hour on /api/web/tools/list from a SINGLE user (~43 req/sec, two bursts under 30s each). It self-resolved, nothing alerted, and nobody noticed. That was 59% of the entire 30-day 500 count in one day. This monitor exists for that.
1. ANY class above 1,000 events/hour, whatever its status. At that rate a human is not generating the traffic and the loop is ours, so status is irrelevant.

2. A 5xx class above 100 events/hour, regardless of blast radius. Pathological volume is an operational symptom even when one customer's server triggered it — an amplification loop is ours no matter whose fault the initiating error was.
3. Any class (4xx or 5xx) at >=20/hour AND >20x its own hourly baseline AND affecting >=3 orgs.

WHY RULE 1 EXISTS — a coverage gap this monitor had for one day. Rules 2 and 3 alone made the 08-06 incident undetectable the moment PR #3948 reclassified upstream auth rejections from 500 to 403: rule 2 needs maxStatus >= 500 (now 403) and rule 3 needs >=3 orgs (08-06 was ONE org). Verified against history — with the 5xx clause removed, replaying 08-06 returns zero rows. Two individually correct changes silently blinded the monitor to its own founding incident.

WHY 1,000: the busiest single 4xx class-hour in 30 days is 142 ('/api/web/tools/* 429' on 2026-07-17); the next is 93. 08-06 was 3,525. A bar of 1,000 sits ~7x above real 4xx traffic and ~3.5x below the incident, so it restores coverage without reintroducing the 429 false page that the maxStatus guard was added to prevent.

WHY 4xx IS INCLUDED BUT GUARDED: classifyRuntimeError checks isUnauthorized401 before every other branch, so MCP auth failures carrying a clean 401 land on http.request.completed and never reach http.request.failed (measured: 2,328 vs 4,932 on /api/web/tools/list). A failed-only view can miss half an incident. But the absolute-volume clause is gated on maxStatus >= 500, because a 4xx is a declared client outcome — only an abnormal RATE of one means anything. Real case that guard prevents: '/api/web/tools/* 429' hit 142/hour on 2026-07-17 and must not page.

maxStatus USES maxif OVER THE RECENT HOUR, NOT max OVER THE WINDOW. The query reads 14 days, so a plain max() would let a single 5xx from days ago satisfy the >= 500 guard while the current burst is entirely 4xx — defeating the guard exactly when it matters. Fingerprints derived from errorMessage can span statuses (the same message under different codes), so this is not hypothetical, merely latent: at the time of writing zero fingerprints spanned both 4xx and 5xx, which is a property of current data rather than a guarantee.

READ THE SHAPE BEFORE THE ERROR. Few orgs with enormous per-org volume is a loop on our side. Many orgs, thin each, is the world being broken — that is a debugger working as intended, and the 147-org 'Couldn't reach the MCP server' class must never page.
NAME THE CLASS (the alert only carries a count):

['inspector-logs'] | where _time > ago(14d) | where event in ('http.request.failed','http.request.completed') | where toint(statusCode) >= 400 | where tostring(environment) in ('prod','production') | extend fpSource = coalesce(tostring(errorMessage), tostring(errorCode), strcat(tostring(route), ' ', tostring(statusCode))) | extend fp = replace_regex(@'[0-9a-z]{20,}', 'ID', substring(fpSource, 0, 100)) | summarize recent = countif(_time > ago(1h)), baseline = countif(_time <= ago(1h)), orgs = dcountif(orgId, _time > ago(1h)), servers = dcountif(serverId, _time > ago(1h)), maxStatus = max(toint(statusCode)) by fp | extend baseHourly = baseline / 335.0, intensity = todouble(recent) / todouble(iff(orgs > 0, orgs, 1)) | where recent >= 20 | sort by intensity desc

TRIAGE: (1) intensity > 100/org/hour means find the LOOP before you find the error — the loop is the outage. (2) Step change at a deploy boundary: check `release` on the failing rows and roll back. (3) Gradual ramp: an upstream is degrading. (4) Do NOT dismiss this because origin says user_config or user_server; this monitor already established the rate is 20x abnormal, and 200x more users did not simultaneously mistype a URL.
COST: measured ~500ms elapsed, 39 blocks, 1.48M rows scanned per evaluation. Cheap at a 15-minute interval; re-measure if the dataset grows materially.

ROLLBACK: revert the definition file, then run `node ops/axiom-monitors/apply.mjs --apply --only inspector-error-class-spike`. The --apply flag is required: the script defaults to read-only plan mode, so omitting it reports the change and leaves the live monitor untouched. If it is noisy, tighten the org/baseline terms rather than raising `recent` — raising the floor is how you go blind to the next 08-06.
